title: Dynamic lane migration pricing experiment for Dedicated capacity
creator: Sofia Morales
description: Context: Enterprise customers need predictable committed GPU capacity plus low-friction burstability. Current reserved SKU model (flat slabs + surge credits) forces either overcommit or expensive ad-hoc surges. This experiment builds a dynamic lane migration pricing model: workload requests are assigned to a lane that represents a commitment band; when demand spikes, the platform can migrate a tenant7s active flows into a higher lane for short durations using Migration Credits (MCs). We will prototype pricing and contract language for migration credits, plus the associated security questionnaire responses (audit, KMS usage, operator controls).
hypothesis: If we price short-term lane migrations via a lightweight credit model and expose migration telemetry in the Console, customers will be able to reduce committed capacity by ~15-25% while keeping p99 latency within SLA and maintaining acceptable cost predictability.
experiment_design: Create three lanes: Base (committed), Headroom (prepaid micro-burst), Surge (on-demand with migration credits).
Introduce Migration Credits (MCs): units consumed per minute of migration at a lane-specific rate; MCs can be prepaid or earned via commitment discounts.
Pilot with 10 existing Dedicated customers (mix of AI startups and mid-market) for 8 weeks: 5 in control (static slab pricing) and 5 in experiment (lane migration enabled).
Instrument Console: surface per-tenant lane occupancy, MC consumption, migration events with start/end timestamps, and fallback actions when MCs depleted.
Contract/Enterprise SQ: draft contract addendum language describing MC accounting, audit access, KMS integration, and operator access restrictions for migration operations.
measurement_plan: Primary metric: committed capacity delta (percent reduction) for experiment cohort vs control over 8 weeks.
SLO metrics: p99 latency by route and by lane; target is < 1.25x baseline p99 during migrations.
Cost predictability: variance in monthly spend (std dev) for experiment vs control.
Adoption signals: percent of eligible requests that used Headroom/Surge lanes and MC utilization rate.
Customer feedback: weekly qualitative check-ins and final NPS delta for pilot customers.
success_criteria: Average committed capacity reduction >= 15% without customer-requested increases to base commitment.
p99 latency degradation during migration events <= 25% relative to baseline and no >5% customer-visible errors attributable to migration.
Customers report pricing predictability is acceptable (>=7/10 in final survey) and are willing to convert MCs to a prepaid/commit option.
Legal and Security signoff on drafted addendum + affirmative answers on enterprise SQ items identified below.
risks: Operational complexity: migrations could increase tail latency if KV cache warming is inadequate; requires engineering mitigation (staggered migration, cache prefetch).
Billing confusion: customers may misunderstand MC consumption leading to billing disputes; need clear Console UI and email alerts.
Contract exposure: new language around forced migrations and capacity handoffs may trigger procurement pushback; legal will need guardrails and opt-outs.
Security: migration involves ephemeral routing changes and potential operator intervention; must ensure RBAC and full audit trail.
acceptance_criteria: Engineering implements lane assignment and migration orchestration with automated rollback for failed migrations.
Console surfaces real-time MC balance and migration timeline for tenant admins.
Billing engine emits clear, line-item MC usage per invoice with links to event IDs for auditing.
Legal reviews and signs off on addendum language; Security reviews auditability and KMS integration and returns < 3 high-severity findings.
sq_items_to_answer: What audit logs are produced for a migration event (requestor, timestamps, pre/post lane states)?
Does migration require cross-region data movement (yes/no) and how is regional residency enforced during migration?
KMS/HSM: are ephemeral keys used for any state transfer and can customers enforce BYOK in migration flows?
Operator access: what minimum role is required to trigger manual migration and what approvals are retained in the audit trail?
SLA language: how do migrations interact with existing p99 latency SLA credits and can migrations be listed as excused events?
decision_log: 2026-03-02: Product approves pilot approach and target cohort selection (Ravi / Sofia).
2026-03-04: Engineering proposes staggered migration to reduce KV-warmup tail; accepted as implementation plan (ENG).
2026-03-08: Legal requests explicit opt-out clause for customers that do not permit automated migrations; agreed for enterprise customers only.
2026-03-09: Security requires per-event HMAC and immutable audit entries; implementation added to scope.
next_steps: Week 1: Finalize pilot cohort and sign NDA/addendum with participating customers (PM + Sales).
Week 2: Shipping milestone - engineering feature branch and basic MC billing plumbing (ENG-21012).
Week 3: Console UX - MC balance card, migration timeline, and alerting (DES handoff).
Week 4: Legal & Security finalize contract text and SQ responses; publish internal playbook for support and dispute triage.
Post-pilot: Create pricing decision framework (keep, iterate, or abandon) and ramp plan for GA if success criteria met.
notes: We intentionally keep MC unit simple (minute-based) for the pilot; if customers prefer tokenized units later we will iterate. Key goal is to validate behavior and contractual acceptance before complex pricing math.
